questions.question:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error.

Jerry driving / home late / when the incident / took place.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the omission of the auxiliary verb "**was**" before the term "**driving**."
 
• In the past continuous tense, which is used to describe an action that was happening at a specific time in the past, the verb "was" is required as an auxiliary for the subject "Jerry."
 
• The correct phrase should be "**Jerry was driving**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 3** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Jerry was driving home late when the incident took place."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "took place." **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **2: "when the incident **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **4: "home late"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

A. at the same time giving happiness to the poor

B. by providing them with food, clothes, money or grain

C. festivals in India are celebrated to share happiness

D. by being in the presence of the members of the family and
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option (4)** i.e. **CDAB**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence begins with the subject "Festivals in India," which is correctly indicated by **part (C).**** **
 
• Following the subject, "are celebrated to share happiness," **(C)** continues the logical sequence, making it clear what the festivals are for.
 
• **The next part,** "by being in the presence of the members of the family and," continues the statement by explaining how happiness is shared, indicated by (D).
 
• **Ending with,** "at the same time giving happiness to the poor by providing them with food, clothes, money or grain" (ABD) completes the sentence by stating the inclusive aspect of festivals in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is **CDAB.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (ACBD):** This option starts with "at the same time giving happiness to the poor by providing them with food, clothes, money or grain." This sequence does not appropriately introduce the subject or flow smoothly.
 
• **Option 2 (CBAD):** This option starts with "festivals in India are celebrated to share happiness by being in the presence of the members of the family and," which places the method before the explanation.
 
• **Option 3 (CABD):** This option disrupts the logical sequence, making the sentence unclear.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The chef prepares the meal with great care.

options.text: The meal was prepared with great care by the chef.
The meal will be prepared with great care by the chef.
The meal is prepared with great care by the chef.
The meal has been prepared with great care by the chef.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The chef prepares the meal with great care."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the meal" at the beginning.
